Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trap'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9); a role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (the Ex-Con's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- An Archivist who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the archive op, which spends the token; code shows them the drawn roles at once, as a night result. Don't tell() the Archivist anything about it.
- Track Arsonist douses with set_status key 'doused' value true. An ignite uses up every douse: clear 'doused' on everyone it hit, survivors included (rules: Arsonist). Don't tell anyone they were doused: code tells the doused players who should know.
- An Auditor who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the audit op; code tells them the player's votes from the Day. Don't tell() the Auditor anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Cartographer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the map op, which spends the token; code tells them the names in that player's group, from your record_visits list. Don't tell() the Cartographer anything about it. It is an Astral Visit: don't put it in record_visits. Code also tells every Cartographer the sizes of tonight's groups, with or without a token, even if role-blocked.
- A Profiler who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the profile op, which spends the token; code tells them the result and tokens left. Don't tell() the Profiler anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- Ritualist who spent tokens (and wasn't role-blocked): compare the guessed role with the target's exact role (a Roleplayer is a Roleplayer). Right: deal the Attack (1 token Standard, 2 Divine). Wrong: no Attack; announce it with tell(['all'], '<name> is a Ritualist.') tonight, which is read out at the start of the next Day, even if the Ritualist dies tonight. Astral Visit.
- Armed (a trait, R24): a player whose trait_actions has trait 'Armed' fires their one hidden-gun shot at its target, in addition to their role's action. It is an action and a visit (R6; record it, and an alerting Veteran's attack hits the shooter): a role-block stops it along with their role's action, and then the shot isn't used. Unless they were role-blocked, use the fire_gun op (it marks the shot used, even if the attack fails) and resolve a Basic Attack on the target (R3): a kill's cause is 'a hidden gun' and its by is the shooter. Tell the shooter only whether their shot killed its target, never the target's role, and tell a surviving target they were attacked.
- Avenger (a trait, R24): when you kill an Avenger at night, code deals a Divine Attack to every player in that kill's `by` who is still alive and kills them (cause 'Avenger'), so list in `by` every player whose attack would have killed them (R12). Don't resolve it yourself; you don't tell() those deaths either.

Moderator strategy review
Strategy reviewThe Village won by hanging the Arsonist on Day 6, but the game came closer than it needed to. The Yakuza were only Bob (Fabricator) and Carol (Ritualist), and they collapsed by Day 3. On Night 1 Erin's profile of Bob came back as Cartographer, Fabricator or Mortician. Alice claimed Cartographer and posted her group sizes. Bob had no other Good option in that profile, so he claimed Cartographer too and copied Alice's sizes exactly. Then he and Carol swapped five daytime private messages that everyone could see. On Night 2 the Yakuza killed Alice, the one player whose claim contradicted Bob's. Alice had the Avenger trait, so Carol died too. Carol was now the confirmed attacker and Bob had copied the dead Cartographer's claim, so Ivan (Sniper) shot Bob on Day 3 and the Yakuza were wiped out. The Ritualist tokens, the Fabricator token and Alice's Armed shot all went unused. After that the only threat was Heidi (Arsonist). She had doused Carol, Alice, Frank and Ivan. Carol and Alice died anyway, so two of her douses were wasted. The Village spent Days 4 and 5 repeating "only hard results" and "post stated votes". They also nominated Frank over how he had worded his Night 3 report, and acquitted him 0-6. Meanwhile Heidi gave no role, no targets and no results until she was pushed late on Day 4. Erin's Night 3 profile of Dave (Archivist, Arsonist or Puppeteer) quietly showed that an Arsonist or a Puppeteer was among the living players, but nobody used it. Grace (Medic) gave only free Standard protection all game and never spent either of her 2 tokens. So Heidi's Strong ignite on Night 5 killed both Frank and Ivan, even though Grace had protected Ivan. With 4 alive, Heidi was the obvious odd one out: she gave empty answers and only stated her watch targets after being nominated. Dave, Erin and Grace convicted her 3-1. Erin had said publicly that she would vote Innocent.

Outside log review (rules and bugs)
Review: medium, harness bugThe setup note says '0 to 3 traits (R24) are dealt to Village players, usually 1 or 2', but this game dealt five trait copies: Alice had Martyr, Armed and Avenger, Erin had Armed, and Grace had Armed. That is only 3 distinct trait types, so either the generator counts types rather than copies (and the setup text needs to say so) or it went over its own limit. Five traits also adds a lot of Village power in a game with only 2 Yakuza and 1 Neutral, which is at odds with 'drawn to help balance the sides'.
Review: medium, player confusionPlayers often lost track of day and night numbers and asked for results from nights that hadn't happened. On Day 3 many players asked for 'Night 3 targets and results' before Night 3. On Day 5 Grace asked for 'any Night 5 result' and Frank said 'My Night 5 audit is set'. On Day 6 Dave asked for 'Night 6 douse, protection and watch targets'. Frank's mixed-up Night 3 status ('audit pending' / 'no audit submitted' / 'no action') then became the whole case for his Day 4 nomination. The prompt could state the phase clearly, e.g. 'Night N comes after Day N; results from the coming night arrive on Day N+1'.
Review: low, player confusionOn Day 6 Erin said Heidi's claimed Night 4 watch on Erin (no visitors) 'checks out with my own no-visit night'. Erin taking no action doesn't show whether anyone visited her, because a Lookout result is about visits to the watched player, so Erin treated the claim as confirmed when nothing confirmed it.
Game over
